report:
FINDINGS:
TENDONS:
SUPRASPINATUS: Moderate supraspinatus tendinosis with low-grade bursal-sided/intrasubstance partial-thickness tear
INFRASPINATUS: The tendon is intact with normal signal intensity.
SUBSCAPULARIS: Mild insertional subscapularis tendinosis without a discrete tear. The tendon is intact with normal signal intensity
TERES MINOR: The tendon is intact with normal signal intensity.
BICEPS BRACHII, LONG HEAD: Moderate long head of the biceps tenosynovitis. The tendon is normally located within the bicipital groove and is intact
LIGAMENTS:
GLENOHUMERAL: The superior, middle, and inferior glenohumeral ligaments are intact.
JOINTS:
GLENOHUMERAL JOINT: Moderate glenohumeral joint effusion with distention of the subscapularis recess. The articular cartilage is preserved
ACROMIOCLAVICULAR JOINT: Moderate acromioclavicular osteoarthrosis with inferior osteophytic spurring
BONES: Small subcortical cystic changes with mild reactive marrow edema in the greater tuberosity. No acute fracture, dislocation, or aggressive osseous lesion
MUSCLES: The rotator cuff muscles demonstrate normal bulk and signal intensity without evidence of atrophy or edema.

OTHER FINDINGS:
mild degenerative fraying of the labrum without a displaced tear
moderate subacromial-subdeltoid bursitis
mild thickening and edema within the rotator interval and inferior glenohumeral capsule

IMPRESSION:
Moderate supraspinatus tendinosis with low-grade bursal-sided/intrasubstance partial-thickness tear, mild insertional subscapularis tendinosis without discrete tear, moderate long head of biceps tenosynovitis, mild degenerative labral fraying without displaced tear, moderate glenohumeral joint effusion with subscapularis recess distention, moderate acromioclavicular osteoarthrosis with inferior osteophytic spurring, moderate subacromial-subdeltoid bursitis, small subcortical cystic changes with mild reactive marrow edema in the greater tuberosity, and mild thickening/edema of the rotator interval and inferior glenohumeral capsule.
